People got on about living wage then started using the numbers in ways they probably should have...

Living wage started out as an argument that in certain metros there was a serious issue where people at the lower end of the spectrum were not able to afford to live in that area, but made far too much money to get assistance. This is a real problem, and could easily be addressed by coming up with better guidelines for where assistance is warranted.

What they probably should have done is start acting like everyone making less than living wage was in some sort of dire circumstance because all they are doing is messing it up for everybody else. Here is why:

  • You won't have much success trying to have different minimum wages in geographically nearby areas, the jobs will just move to the other area
  • Minimum wage from an employer's perspective is effectively the legal limit of what you must automate. If I need my phones answered I could hire a receptionist for all-in cost of around $30k/yr (minimum wage with all the required taxes, legally mandated training and minimum benefits) or I could buy a new phone system for about $120k. I hire the receptionist. But if the receptionist costs around $63k/yr maybe I buy the phone system.
  • The crusaders on this one are pretty much running with the assumption that everyone is living by themselves and/or made the bad decision to have a child before they were financially ready. I don't know about anyone else, but I always had roommates when I was broke, and their are plenty of places in the states where minimum is enough if you have roommates - http://livingwage.mit.edu/counties/54093 or http://livingwage.mit.edu/counties/39075 for example.
  • If these folks ever get any traction across the country you are just going to see costs rise as all the jobs in-between minimum and new-minimum rates will have to adjust or lose their staff and that will just ripple upward. This exacerbates the loss in jobs from the second point

The smart argument here would be for government benefits to those incapable of ever achieving more than minimum wage to go along with the already established benefits for children in lower income situations as that is a much smaller minority and probably the folks that actually need the assistance since there is obviously something needing fixed there.
